utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge that enables you to explain or comment on the fact that Bosniaks where you lived regarded this as a war in which they did not wish to take part, but it seems possible that Bosniaks living in Croatia did respond to a mobilisation call there and participate in that very war? Do you have any knowledge that enables you to comment on that apparent difference?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no such knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And do you agree that if the Serb community in your area came to believe that Muslims were fighting for the Croatian Army while refusing to respond to mobilisation for the JNA, that that would have further embittered relations between the Bosniak and the Serb community where you lived?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: This calls for speculation on behalf of the witness. And more than that, it calls for speculation on behalf of the witness in respect of facts that have not been established. So we would ask the Defence again to move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I prefaced my question very carefully asking the witness -- my first question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's a hypothetical question, "If the Serb community in your area came to believe that ..." That's a hypothesis. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I don't feel it necessary to pursue it and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, that was as a matter of fact would be my question, what exactly the point is, because I was about to ask the Prosecution whether there's any disagreement on that the relations between the two ethnic groups became more and more bitter for, well, whatever reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't need to pursue the question. It can be a comment in a hundred years from now. It doesn't need to be a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, the document in front of you that we were looking at a few minutes ago, moving right on to the passage that you were asked about, section VI, the course of armed operations, I'd like you to find that heading, please. I think it was page 8 of the B/C/S version. I hope that's not misleading you. Do you see that heading, "The course of armed operations"?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I just want to use that as a marker. I want you to look one paragraph up from that at the paragraph that begins: "All of our findings point to the fact that the Muslim TO ..." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you find it, Mr. Egrlic? It's the part that starts --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've found it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: "All our findings point to the fact that the Muslim TO was primarily set up for defence purposes. However, investigations through operational work later established that several meetings were held in Prijedor and Sanski Most in May where they adopted the decision to commence armed rebellion in order to achieve their already mentioned goals. The decision to change the concept from defensive to offensive operations had a catastrophic effect on the Muslim population in the area of Kljuc Municipality. The attacks they launched on 27th May 1992 of Kljuc Municipality. The attacks they launched on 27th May 1992 gave proper cause to the members of the Bosnia-Herzegovina Serbian Republic Army to settle accounts by taking determined action against the perpetrators of and participants in these acts." Now, first of all, Mr. Egrlic, do you agree with this observation that the Muslim TO was primarily set up for defence purposes?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have spoken about this already. And the Muslim Territorial Defence, as you like to call it, was the Territorial Defence of the State of Bosnia and Herzegovina that was set up as an organised TO staff. It was getting ready to set up some units. However, in view of the late appointment of that staff, the units were never established. Therefore, there was no concept even of what kind of war should be waged, a defensive one or a conqueror's war.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: All right. Now, Mr. Egrlic, you were asked about the first paragraph under heading VI beginning: "Armed operations in the area of Kljuc Municipality began on the 27th of May 1992." You were asked about that paragraph. I would like you, please, to look at the words at the end of that paragraph, "The following occurred on that day." And then to --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I hope it's acceptable to say to the witness to read to himself. It's rather a long passage. I'm in Your Honours' hands. I wasn't proposing to read it all out. But of course, if Your Honour feels I should, I will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. Up to where would you like him to read?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I would like him to read the whole passage. It's about 20 or 30 lines. It just goes over the foot of the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Item 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Item 1, under the heading: "Setting up an ambush in the Gornji Ramici sector."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'm in Your Honour's hands as to how I deal with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the witness is now invited to read for himself what appears in the English translation on page 6 under heading VI.1, "Setting up an ambush in the Gornji Ramici sector" up to the second paragraph on page 7 where it starts "setting up an ambush in the..." Mr. Egrlic, once you've finished reading -- I take it you're reading page 9 in the B/C/S version entirely and the first three lines of page 10. Once you've finished, please tell me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, do you say that none of that is true?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's true this incident happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Is there any significant error in the account which you have just read?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about these details. But I don't [as interpreted] know that it happened on the 27th of May, that much I heard. I don't know the exact details of what happened so I can't say anything with any certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for the transcript, it reads "I don't know about these details." And then it continues "but I don't know that it happened on the 27th of May." Did you want to say that you do know that it happened on the 27th of May? It might be a translation problem.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that I did know that it happened, but that I didn't know all the details. I didn't know many details about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: According to your knowledge, it happened on the 27th of May?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. This is just to correct the transcript which, of course, we receive your words in translation, and sometimes there is some confusion. It's not due to you. But please proceed, Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'm obliged, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: The next item, it's mercifully much shorter, item 2, "Setting up an ambush in the Busije and" - well, it's illegible. Perhaps it doesn't matter too much - "sectors." Again, could you read that and let His Honour and the rest of the Court know when you're finished reading it.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Did those events happen as they are described there?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As to whether they occurred on the same day, I had information about that. But I don't know about these details because I wasn't involved in this. I wasn't present.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So is it the position that you can't say that any of it is false, but you don't know yourself of whether all of it is true. Is that a fair summary, Mr. Egrlic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can't say whether it's true or not, whether it's correct or not. But I know that this occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Leaving aside details, it's essentially true; an incident broadly as described here did occur?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Could I invite you, Mr. Egrlic, to read 3, 4, 5, and 6 all at one go, because they're pretty short passages. So following on from where we just got to, could you read the next passages, 3, 4, 5, and 6, and let His Honour know when you've done that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While the witness reads, could I ask the Prosecution whether it would change anything in their case if these, I would say, lists of incidents even if committed by Bosniaks as they were called recently had occurred?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, shouldn't the witness take his headphones for such a question, we suggest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Certainly to hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Given where we are at the moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, our case is not concerned with combat operations. And whilst I'm not in a position to comment in an informed way about each of these alleged events, insofar as combat operations took place in the municipality, that's not the focus of our case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you consider these to be combat operations or ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm unable to say whether or not they are because I haven't had the opportunity to investigate whether or not they occurred or any other corroborative or contradictory information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm just wondering whether this seems to be at least not the core of the case of the Prosecution, how important it is that we spend quite a lot of time on it, especially where the witness has I think for the first two incidents said that they may well -- that they occurred; whether or not with all the details. If the witness would say the same for the next three or four, of course, I do not know whether he will, but would that cause the Prosecution to take any further procedural action on it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is certainly not the core of our case, and we don't know whether or not the tu quoque defence is something that the Defence is considering raising.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I suggest that -- because we do get an answer, but not exactly on the question I put to the Prosecution. Perhaps just as some guidance, next time you could have just asked: "This report describes a couple of actions which are described as attacks by Muslims including this, this, and this, and do you agree they took place? Yes or no." That would have approximately the same result especially since it's not in the core of the case. I mean, this case is not about who fired the first shot and at what moment and against whom, but mainly on what happened later. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, with respect, I agree. I simply say this, Your Honour, first of all, I couldn't ask the witness to give that answer without giving him an opportunity of reading what it was he was being asked to answer upon. The second observation, Your Honour, is that we could have had his answer on points 3, 4, 5, 6 in less time. And the third point, Your Honour, as far as first shots are concerned, the Prosecution asked about the introductory paragraph of this section. If they had not asked about the introductory paragraph which leads us naively Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond to suppose it might be part of their case, we might not have found it necessary to go on to ask questions about the rest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please put your headphones on again. Have you read the relevant parts, Mr. Egrlic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've read parts 3, 4, 5, and 6, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Are they true?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is stated under item 3, 4, and 5, I couldn't say. I've heard about the event described under number 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So you've heard it described in, for practical purposes, the same terms as you see under item 6, have you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I certainly can leave that topic now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'm entirely in Your Honour's hands as to whether the break will come. I can never quite remember when it's half past or 25 past that Your Honour favours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, you've got the morning schedule in your mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Top of the hour. Wishful thinking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll adjourn anywhere between 20 minutes to 6.00 up till a quarter to 6.00. After 20 minutes' break, we'll have another hour to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I think Your Honour is right. It's that bit of the clock I was thinking of in morning hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It took me two years as well, Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour has helped me to get there quicker. I'll try and remember another day.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, you were -- I wonder if you could be given a document. It has not so far been an exhibit in the course of this witness's evidence or in this case, Your Honour. We have copies in both B/C/S and English, of course. The original is in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The next number, Mr. Registrar, would be, for the Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the number will be D24.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And D24.1 for the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Would Your Honour give me one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Loukas reminds me very reasonably Your Honour that perhaps I should say is the only reason we haven't supplied this in advance is that our reading of it and our decision to use it has been so recent that the opportunity simply didn't arise. So with that apology, here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Egrlic, I -- the simplest thing is for me to invite you first of all just to have a quick look at this document. And before we -- just sufficiently to answer the question whether you have ever seen this document or a copy of this document before?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart, as a matter of fact, what has been presented to us are actually two documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore -- and they very much look the same. So if you're asking about a document, could you please guide the witness to look at what exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, Ms. Loukas had just helpfully reminded me that there were the two B/C/S versions. Does the witness at the moment just have -- perhaps he can have both. They are quite similar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It's the same -- as far as we can see, it's the same document, but it has been transmitted on different occasions, so towards the top of the page it bears different markings indicating that it has been transmitted. Is that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It also has different markings in the text, Mr. -- If you would look at the underlining, you would see that there are differences as well. So could you please tell us whether you would like the witness to look at the copy with two underlined segments on the bottom or the one underlined?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: My question, Mr. Egrlic, is just have a fairly quick look, please, at both of them, and please tell Their Honours whether you remember seeing either of these documents, or a copy of either of these documents before.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I've seen these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Just to make it clear, it's in fact, with some differences of underlining and some markings towards the top of the page, in its essentials, the text is the same? It's basically the same document? You can see that, Mr. Egrlic, can't you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what one would say on the basis of the contents.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, I take the one, just for convenience, so that we're all working from the same one, Mr. Egrlic, I invite you to take the one that has got two lots of underlining. So in items 4 and 5, in each of those you will see some underlining. If you take that one and if everybody looks at that one for the moment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can we get rid of the other one.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I believe we can, Your Honour. It really isn't going to -- certainly, Your Honour got rid of it in comprehensive terms. That's the sound of copies being got rid of that's being recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, it's -- I'm, of course, now reading from the English. But it's headed on the top left, leaving aside the stuff that's to do with it being faxed backwards and forwards "Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Ministry of National Defence, Territorial Defence staff, Sarajevo." There's a date, 29th of April 1992. "Very urgent. Order to carry out the decision of the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina." And I did ask you to look quickly at it a few minutes ago, Mr. Egrlic. But just taking a little bit more slowly now, then, "On the basis of the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina's decision of 27th of April 1992 on the withdrawal of JNA/Yugoslav People's Army units from the territory of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and because of the violation of this Presidency decision and because the former JNA has begun to steal and plunder the property of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, I hereby issue the following..." And taking it in summary rather than reading it all out subject to His Honour's direction, mount a blockade of all roads, number one; number two, mount a blockade of the wider and make use of natural obstacles; three, to prevent unannounced columns of units of the former JNA unescorted by the MUP from leaving their barracks; four, speed up combat activities. I'm summarising. And then finishing up, combat operations, plans should include extensive measures for the protection of the population and the material goods of the citizens of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And it's signed by Commander, Colonel Hasan Efendic. Now, in April 1992, you knew who Mr. Efendic was, didn't you, Mr. Egrlic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew because he had designated a commander of the Territorial Defence in Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Now, you were informed by Mr. Omer Filipovic of the contents of this document, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't inform me about the contents. This is the first time I've seen the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So you're saying, Mr. Egrlic, two not exactly the same things. You've never seen this document before, and are you saying that you'd never even heard about it before?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about it when I came here and read Mr. Filipovic's statement according to which there was some kind of a document. But I never had the opportunity to examine the document. This is the first time I have seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, let's look again, please, at Mr. Filipovic's statement, which is the one you just mentioned you read.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: That is an exhibit in this case. That's P245, if the witness might be handed that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And Mr. Filipovic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Mr. Filipovic had a position within the TO, Territorial Defence, didn't he, in April 1992?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: He was the commander in -- he was the commander in Pudin Han. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Which we know is within the Municipality of Kljuc. Look again at his statement at -- excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that you would lead the witness to page 2, the last five lines to start with, and then to continue page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. It's the last paragraph on page 2 of the English version. I was just inviting Ms. Cmeric to tell me exactly where it was in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It's in the middle of page -- slightly higher up, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's the last --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It's about five lines from the bottom of page 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I referred to.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I thank you. Your Honour is ahead of me getting my information from my left. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: But I think perhaps we better start just a little higher up at the beginning of that -- well, that's where you are in the B/C/S version. "Among the mentioned written instructions that I can remember..." Do you see that paragraph, Mr. Egrlic? First of all, whether you see the paragraph, Mr. Egrlic, and then I shall feel happier if I know you've got the right paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness starts reading the paragraph where on the first line "the 29th of April" appears.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, which page is that on?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: On page 2 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: On page 2, His Honour is suggesting, Mr. Egrlic, that you begin at a paragraph on page 2. It's somewhere in the bottom half of page 2 that has the date "29th of April" in the first line. It says "after a short period of time, I think it was on 29th April this year ..." Do you see that? You're being helped to it, Mr. Egrlic. You've got that, have you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So "after a short period of time, I think it was on the 29th of April I sent the proposal or I received a fax message addressed to the vice-president of the Kljuc Municipal Assembly."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Counsel, please slow down for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: "But it was by mistake given to the president of the municipal assembly and the executive committee. I think that the copy of this fax is filed at the information centre. I lost my copy. It is stated in the fax that by order I" - that's Filipovic - "am appointed commander of the TO staff of the Kljuc Municipality, the order on my appointment was signed by TO Bosnia-Herzegovina commander Colonel Hasan Efendic. All my contacts with the TO BH staff involved only a few of my telephone calls and a few of their telephone messages and orders." And then it goes on: "Among the mentioned written instructions that I can remember are instruction or something else - I do not recall exactly the name of the document - for work of the TO units. I think also directive for disabling and preventing unannounced military columns, former JNA, to pass and some other less important instructions. We were ordered to prevent and disable unannounced persons and persons without escort of the BH MUP police to pass. I cannot recall the exact words of the order, but I think it said that all devices at our disposal should be used to implement the task." Now, would you agree so far, Mr. Egrlic, that that document just described there by Mr. Filipovic is about as clearly as can be the document we've just been looking at?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The conclusion one would draw on the basis of this description is that this is the document in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. It then continues: "Directive and other documentation can be found in the centre in the village of Pudin Han. I informed the president of the executive committee, Asim Egrlic, about the contents of the directive." So, are you now saying that he is wrong about that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have already said, he didn't inform me about this, and today is the first time I've seen this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So just to get it clear, he is wrong about that, then, in that statement?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Do you -- that statement is dated 29th of May 1992. Mr. Egrlic, you were asked specifically by the Prosecution whether you'd had an opportunity to read this statement. This was at page 62 of yesterday's transcript. You said, "Yes, I have." And you were asked: "In general terms to the best of your knowledge and matters you had knowledge on, is this statement accurate?" And your answer was: "For the most part, the greatest part of the statement, it is." Can you explain why you gave that confirmation to the Trial Chamber yesterday when this particular point in the statement involving yourself is wrong?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: If we could refer to the bottom of page 63 of the Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond transcript of yesterday, you'll see that the answer the witness gave yesterday is entirely consistent with the answer he has given today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that this was exactly the spot he referred to as being incorrect in the statement of Mr. Filipovic, Mr. Stewart. But we could check.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. It's at the bottom of page 63, and the answer is given at the top of page 64.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just checking.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, I've no answer to that one, Your Honour. That's obviously -- what Mr. Margetts says is clearly correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, my apologies. I'd simply overlooked it, and that's absolutely right. Good point for a break, Your Honour, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. This needs some reflection. We'll have a break until 5 minutes past 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, you -- jumping to a different topic altogether, you told the Trial Chamber on Tuesday when you gave your evidence, and this is at page 35 of the transcript, that you had first heard of the crisis staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina around mid-1991. And my question is how sure you are of that particular time period, mid-1991?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said I thought it was in mid-1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: You say you thought. So would you be surprised, then, to know that there was no Autonomous Region of Krajina Crisis Staff at any time during 1991?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether I would be surprised, but I think that it was already established in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: But if I suggest to you that it wasn't actually established until April 1992, is it that you wouldn't be in a position to say that was wrong?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be because after all many years have passed since. All I was able to say was that I thought it happened in that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, I meant May, but I don't think that affects your answer, Mr. Egrlic. The -- you talked about Mr. Brdjanin, and you described him communicating with the SDS representatives in Kljuc by using the fax, et cetera, is what you said -- well, on the phone, by using the fax, et cetera. And then you were asked about a particular document, the one with the 14 points which we'll come to in due course. But is that particular communication, the document that we looked at with the 14 points - do say if you feel the need to see it right now - is that the only specific communication that you know of between Mr. Brdjanin and the SDS representatives in Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for written documents, it is the only document attesting to the fact of communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Do you have any specific recollection, knowledge of any other communication between Mr. Brdjanin and the SDS representatives in Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I wonder if you could be handed, please, the document which is Exhibit P228. Now, you said that the contents of the document seem to amount to introducing a state of emergency which was only appropriate in a time of war. That was your answer. That's page 38 of Tuesday's transcript. Do you agree that on the 29th of October 1991, this was a document which was produced in a time of war?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the area of Kljuc Municipality and in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina, this was not wartime. The war was going on in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: But this document is -- talks about the war in Croatia, doesn't it, Mr. Egrlic? See point 14.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: That's an express reference to Croatia. Look at point 3, "Form units for the front and designate their replacements." What "front" do you say was being referred to there?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a reference to the Croatian front, but it was necessary -- not necessary for that purpose to form a command in our place and abrogate the power that belonged to local authorities. And that was in item 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So let's get it clear, then, Mr. Egrlic: The answer you've just given implies your disagreement [Realtime transcript read in error "agreement"] with the authors of this document about what was necessary at the time. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: That question fails to accurately specify what the witness said. Defence counsel has characterised one element of the witness's answer, but has neglected to characterise the second element of the answer. The second --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The answer of the witness is not properly summarised by only referring to what he deemed to be necessary. He also said that this was within the power of local authorities and not to, I take it, at least, the persons or authority that sent this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: With respect, Your Honour, partly. One difficulty is I think there's an error in the transcript because I say: "So let's get it clear, then, Mr. Egrlic, the answer you've just given implies your agreement with the authors of this document" and I think the word should be "disagreement". Just to clear that up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's what I heard you say.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: That's a side detail, but just to make that clear. But Your Honour then there's nothing unfair or inappropriate about my question because I'm not attempting and I don't need to summarise the whole answer. The point which I then ask in my further question is an entirely fair point to take from the answer because the answer contains two limbs. And I'm not -- there's no distortion and there's no unfairness in my concentrating a further question on that particular element of the previous answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Margetts. I do agree that you said, "This answer you've given implies" which of course is a rather vague thing. Would you say include or -- yes, Mr. Margetts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MARGETTS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Defence has characterised the witness's disagreement with the authorities to be in respect of the necessity; the witness has clearly said that the disagreement is in respect of the necessity and in respect of the illegality.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: That demonstrates that my question is an entirely fair one because I'm entitled to take those points separately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But -- well, it's a bit -- Mr. Stewart, let me perhaps use an example that's not directly related to this one, although it was very recently. When the witness said it was -- there was no war, look at number 14. There they're talking about war. This, of course, is a way of questioning -- I mean, if I would put it to you that wherever war is reported on the radio that would equal more or less a situation of war, you will certainly agree with me that that's not a fair way of putting it to a witness. I mean, it's perhaps within the art of cross-examination which, as you may know, is not appreciated in all its aspects in all systems. Therefore, I'd like to ask you to make clear if you're dealing with one part of the answer of the witness or another part because it could confuse the witness, and we want to avoid that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, with all due respect, I think it's the objection and the exchange which has confused the witness because there wasn't apparently any confusion on the part of the witness before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I said I was afraid it might confuse the witness. And you may now proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It's your belief, Mr. Egrlic, that the steps set out in this document were not necessary at that time in Kljuc. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: The answer you gave on Tuesday was that a state of emergency -- well, it amounted to introducing a state of emergency which was only appropriate in a time of war.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Is it then your -- is this a fair summary of what you're saying, that you didn't regard Kljuc as being in a time or state of war?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't. I said so several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: You said in your evidence on Tuesday that on the basis of this document, a number of steps were taken by the SDS, the Serbian Democratic Party so that in the forthcoming period these items were implemented. And by "implemented," did you intend to mean implemented in Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Kljuc, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And in fact, in your evidence, you were asked, "Were most of the items listed numbered 1 to 14 implemented by the Kljuc SDS?" And you said: "Yes." And you stand by that answer, do you, Mr. Egrlic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So item 1, "Immediately form a command of the town and set up round-the-clock duty," was that done immediately after the 29th of October 1991?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was. Soon after.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: How soon after?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think a couple of days later, the command of the town was formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that the crisis staff had been formed. That's what I mean when I mentioned this command of the town, because by establishing the crisis staff, they took upon themselves all the functions of the municipal assembly and the legally elected authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So that was done within a couple of days. And was round-the-clock duty set up at the same time?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Round-the-clock duty was introduced with relation to executive authorities, the police, and the army. The number of troops on the streets, the number of personnel on the streets was increased, and duty service was stepped up.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Let's be very specific, Mr. Egrlic: When do you say that you first heard about or knew that a command of the town, in the sense that you've described it, had been set up by the SDS?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that even before this date. The War Presidency had been established, or rather, the Crisis Staff of the Serbian Democratic Party which later evolved into the War Presidency.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: In Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Kljuc, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Please let's be very specific about the question and the answer, of course, Mr. Egrlic. You are telling the Tribunal that within a couple of days - that was your phrase - after this document, a command of the town - I'm just using the phrase in the English translation which I suppose gets translated back to the original Serbian - you say that was formed. When did you first know that that had happened?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought that these other items had been implemented within a couple of days. As far as the command of the town is concerned, or rather, the crisis staff, I know that the crisis staff existed even before this date. And when I say "crisis staff," I imply the command of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Did anything change then so far as crisis staff, command of the town? Did anything change after the 29th of October 1991?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What changed is that mobilisation call-ups of the Territorial Defence became more frequent. Units began to be sent to Croatia officially. It was no longer volunteer units --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, I'm going to stop you and invite you to stick to the questions. We have been for some minutes now very clearly talking about item 1 on this list. And it was your evidence before this Trial Chamber that these items on the list were implemented, most of the items number 1 to 14 were implemented. And I was careful to make it clear that at this point I was talking specifically about item 1, and you specifically said "a couple of days later." If you want to change your answer, Mr. Egrlic, you've given the solemn declaration, you must change your answer if you feel that's the right thing to do. So far as item 1 on that list as you understand it, was there any change within a few days or a couple of weeks after the 29th of October 1991 in Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And what was that change?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mobilisation of conscripts became more frequent. There was takeover of power in enterprises in the social accounting service, the SDK.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll stop you for a second, Mr. Egrlic. Mr. Stewart has asked you to concentrate exclusively on item 1 which reads: "Immediately form a command of the town and set up round-the-clock duty." That's what Mr. Stewart asked you about. And the core of his question is that where you said that this was implemented a couple of days later, in an answer a few lines further, you said, well, actually there was already something like that. There was already a command or there was a crisis staff. What Mr. Stewart wants to know from you, was this formation of a command of the town and the setting up round-the-clock duty, was that implemented a couple of days later or was that already in existence when, on the 29th of October, this order was delivered? That's the core of his question. Could you answer to that, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for the command of the town, it had already been formed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore, his question then was what did then change after the 29th of October if it was already formed? Exclusively on formation of the command of the town, the setting up round-the-clock duty, did anything change in that respect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the command of the Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond town was not formed just for the sake of forming it. I'm talking about the activities that followed after.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do I then understand your testimony until now where you twice started saying that the mobilisation that became, as you said it -- let me just have a look. That that became more frequent, that you wanted to tell us that the command of the town already in existence took measures as we find them, other measures we find on that list in view of mobilisation, you said, and the takeover of power in enterprises, is that how I have to understand your answer? So already in existence, but the other items, at least you mentioned two, that changed after the 29th of October.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And so item 2, the "Establish full mobility of the Territorial Defence," when do you say that happened?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This, too, had been underway even before the order. The order only contributed to the building up of the mobilisation and establishment of units.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And did -- had you -- you had been aware of that, had you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the citizens were aware of that. People went to the battlefield by bus. They would go there and return. People were released from companies on paid leave. That was not a secret in Kljuc, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And when do you say that that happens? When do you say it began?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It began in August and continued after that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And what in your view was wrong with that, as a step to have been taken?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was all wrong. First of all, people would leave their jobs. Secondly, it was a way of arming Serbian soldiers. Weapons weren't returned. They would take the weapons home with them. Thirdly, the peace was disturbed in Kljuc because they would go to the front with the weapons, and when they returned they would disturb and unsettle the citizens. There was nothing good about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Those were the consequences, Mr. Egrlic. But your answer: "All the citizens were aware of that people went to the battlefield by bus." I take it this is correct, when you say "the battlefield," you mean the battlefield in and with Croatia. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I don't want to go over the same old ground again, Mr. Egrlic. But there was a war on, so people were going to the battlefield, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They went to the battlefield, but it was in a different republic, and the Municipality of Kljuc is in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I'm talking about the situation in the Municipality of Kljuc, and I'm talking about the consequences of frequent mobilisation, the consequences of the citizens being disturbed. I'm not talking about some sort of municipality in Croatia. I'm talking about a municipality in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: The third item, "Form units for the front and designate their replacements," was that done?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And when was that done?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was done immediately after this decision was made. And earlier on, too, as I have said. This decision only reinforced this matter and it continued in this manner until May.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: How was the war in Croatia to be fought without units being formed for the front?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a question you should put to the people who fought in the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Let me rephrase the question, then. In your view, because you have commented quite a lot on this document, and it's part of your evidence, your comments, in your view, how was the war to be fought without forming units for the front?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my view, there shouldn't have been a war at all. I have said this on a number of occasions. And I didn't support this war, nor did the policies of the Bosniak people because this is what caused the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Item 4, "All men under the age of 40 to be reassigned from civilian protection to Territorial Defence and Territorial Defence to be subordinated to the corps as wartime units." Did that happen?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: You know that, do you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: How do you know it?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know that because in the secretariat for national defence, there was a clerk who was still working there. He was a Bosniak, and he told me that as far as the cards, et cetera, were concerned, this should be done, and these units for fighting in the battlefield in Croatia should be formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And when did you first come to know about that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I came to know about that sometime in November 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Item 5 on the list: "Take over management in public enterprises, the post office, SDK public auditing service, bank, judiciary, and by all means" - is the translation - "the media." Did that happen?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in some of the companies, it did happen. In others, it didn't because Serbs already occupied the posts there. I said that yesterday or the day before yesterday. I don't remember when. As far as the media is concerned, Asmir Burzic was replaced and a Serb took his place. In the SDK, the public auditing service, a Bosniak was similarly replaced and a Serb took his place. So the Serbs replaced the Bosniaks, and this decision is one that was implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: When did this process as described in point 5 then -- when did it first begin?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it started after this order, immediately after the order. And as there weren't Bosniaks in these places, it was quite easy to bring it to an end.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: When did the process -- when was it completed? Point 5, we're still talking about.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was completed on the 7th of May 1992 when all the Bosniaks were brutally dismissed from all their jobs in the territory of the Municipality of Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: What about 6, "Proclaim a wartime programme schedule on radio stations." Was that done?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Immediately after the radio station was taken over and when the editor was replaced, this wartime programme began to be implemented. And this occurred at the very beginning of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Point 7: "In each municipality, call a meeting of all directors and agree on the means of supplying the population with everything from electricity to consumer goods." Did that happen?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: When did it happen?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning of 1992, all the directors were summoned, and they were issued orders and instructed about what they should do. This depended on the type of trade concerned, and they were told what they had to provide, to supply the troops, citizens, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Were you present at any such meeting?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Can you say when you -- well, how many meetings between October 1991 and -- end of October 1991 and beginning of May 1992, how many such meetings did you attend?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only attended one such meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Point 8: "Place a moratorium on the issuing of construction permits, sale of plots of land, election of directors where the absence of reservists is being abused and halt all changes of ownership of enterprises, et cetera." Did that happen in Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Was there -- specifically, was there an abuse of the absence of reservists in Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This started when they returned from the battlefield with their weapons. They started shooting from their weapons and entering shops.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Point number 9: "The employment of" - well, there were two elements top point number 9. I will deal with both. "The employment of able-bodied persons from war regions is strictly banned." So that's point number 1. And then coupled with that, "if there are any such already employed, they should be fired immediately and returned to the front." Did that happen in Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were refugees in Kljuc who had found accommodation in the hotel. They were from the territory of Croatia. Able-bodied men were mobilised and sent back to the battlefields in Croatia together with other reservists.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So there was a strict ban, was there, and all such able-bodied persons were fired immediately in Kljuc, were they?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They weren't employed. They had been mobilised. As they were in the hotel, that is where they were staying, and they were mobilised for the purposes of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Point 10: "All weapons and equipment to be collected from deserters." Did that happen?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That didn't happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Were there deserters?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Number 11: "Make lists of surplus goods as well as shortages and inform SDS Sarajevo, Mr. Ilic, about this." First of all, were such lists made?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were lists in shops. And yes, such lists were made.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Who made them?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were made by commissions from trading companies.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Did you ever see any such list?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. But I do know that lists were made.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Do you know who Mr. Ilic was?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Do you know whether he was ever given any information about any of this stuff in point 11?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Number 12 is "Paramilitary formations, if they exist, to be disbanded immediately and reassigned to the Territorial Defence. This must be carried out without fail." Were there paramilitary formations on the 29th of October 1991 in Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not on that date. But after the new year, some sort of Bijeli Orlovi or White Eagles arrived. I don't know whether they were resubordinated to the Territorial Defence, but they were present in the territory of the Municipality of Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: How long after the new year did they arrive?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps it was in February. Before them, some sort of Red Beret formations came to that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: After the new year, but before them?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The White Eagles came after the new year. But the Red Berets were there before them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, but before or after the new year, Mr. Egrlic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the new year. The Red Berets came before the new year, whereas the White Eagles came after the new year.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: How long before the new year did the Red Berets arrive?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was around November.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Were they disbanded at any point after their arrival?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they weren't. They remained in the territory of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Point 13: "Impose also war taxes for greater success of the entire operation." Did that happen in Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This item is closely linked to item 7 where it says: "Summon all directors in the municipalities and agree on how the population should be provided with supplies. Work organisations had the duty to assist the Serbian Army by providing them with certain supplies. And I think that this concerns the so-called war taxes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour can see that I'm coming up to item 14. I did ask to have five minutes please at some point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, as I a matter of fact I promised before or after the last break. And of course, when you were halfway, I thought there would be five minutes left until 14. But I don't know how important 14 for you is. But I would give you five minutes now. Since I assume that it's important for you to have the five minutes now and not tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand. Mr. Egrlic, we're not finished yet as you may have understood. We would like to see you back. But tomorrow we are sitting in the morning again, so that would be at 9.00 tomorrow morning. And I again instruct you not to speak with anyone about the testimony you've given in this Court or you're still about to give although you might not know what it is about. But speak with no one about your situation as a witness. Mr. Usher, may escort Mr. Egrlic out of the courtroom. We would like to see you back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, I'm much obliged, Your Honour. Of course, it would have been neater if I had finished the 14. It's not important. It's really just like having pencils in a row on the desk. Your Honour, there are two points I wanted to raise. The first one was very brief. It was in relation to the observations made by my client Mr. Krajisnik earlier. Simply to say that of course it's not appropriate and the Trial Chamber wouldn't expect it to be privy to discussions in any detail that take place between Mr. Krajisnik and myself, but just to tell Your Honour that we have given no advice -- I can say this, we have given no advice to Mr. Krajisnik which is inconsistent with the outline that Your Honour gave as to the various responsibilities and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I've understood all the observations made by Mr. Krajisnik as an expression of his own concerns about several aspects of his own involvement in the preparation of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. But I wanted to assure Your Honour for the purposes of, if you like, good order of such matters and how they will be dealt with, Your Honour can see how they would be likely to be dealt with. Your Honour, the second observation, it is the only other observation on what Mr. Krajisnik says is then linked to the question of the motion that Mr. Krajisnik offered or suggested what might be an alternative if he were not able to have the transcripts. I do wish to emphasise, Your Honour, that we on Mr. Krajisnik's behalf actually regard that as a most unsatisfactory alternative, whether it's a second-best, third-best or fourth-best, the idea that Mr. Krajisnik, by bringing a computer into court, that in any way remotely solves the difficulty which we say can only be fairly solved with the transcripts, we don't endorse that, and we really understand Mr. Krajisnik to be saying that. But his observation was if you like in pessimistic anticipation of the possibility that the motion might not succeed on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course, we never understood this observation of Mr. Krajisnik to replace or to be second-best to having, but I did understand it, and I think my fellow Judges also did to say that if the motion would fail, then it would certainly assist me if I would at least have a laptop computer in court so that I could at least process whatever I'd like to process, information, in a better way as I'm able to do now. That's how I understood. So it's not -- the Chamber will certainly -- you don't have to fear, Mr. Stewart, that the Chamber will say, well, since a very nice alternative has presented by Mr. Krajisnik himself, that could -- that convince us that otherwise we would do as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, I'm grateful, Your Honour. Clearly a laptop is better than no laptop from Mr. Krajisnik's point of view. I'm very happy to hear Your Lordship - whether that's a promotion or demotion, I'm not sure, Your Honour. I'm sure it's greatly merited in any case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it's clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. On what you call the B/C/S motion for shorthand, Your Honour, we, of course, have indicated that it would be -- it would be most helpful to have a decision particularly on the point about the transcripts. On the other hand, of course, we are primarily concerned about getting what we regard as the right decision, that's our submission, Your Honour, of course. And if the Prosecution -- if the position is the Prosecution have simply asserted their global position and that's all it is, and it's not particularised in any way, we therefore don't have any opportunity to respond, which would be the normal course, to any points they make, it doesn't become an entirely satisfactory way of dealing with this very important point, Your Honour. We would have a preference, although we would like it dealt with as soon as possible, but we would in fact have a preference if it is necessary to have the matter thoroughly ventilated and to know exactly what the points are, and so far as resource implications are relied upon by anybody, what those implications might be, we would prefer it to be later rather than sooner, if I might say that. Our preference is to have it thoroughly aired rather than have it dealt with very urgently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may take it from the questions I put at the beginning of this hearing to you that the Chamber has, of course, already paid a lot of attention to your motion and I expect that the Chamber will be able to give an oral decision by tomorrow. But of course, finally, we have to reach a final decision. And if it could not be a full decision, then at least on the most important elements of the motion you indicated before to me. Yes. We'll then adjourn with, again, thanks to the interpreters, but also to the technicians, and we'll adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00, same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 30th day of July, 2004, at 9.00 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
